# 生產者物價降溫，美債續漲，長端仍有阻力

## 通膨再傳好消息，經濟尚未明顯失速

繼前一天消費者物價低於預期後，生產者物價也出現下跌，美國公債連續第二天上漲。買盤仍集中在較短天期：2年期與5年期殖利率各降5個基點，30年期則持平。市場估計7月升息機率已降至約10%，遠低於CPI公布前的約40%。

這波行情並不是由需求全面轉弱帶動。紐約州製造業的新訂單、出貨與就業同步改善，聯準會褐皮書也顯示經濟仍在溫和擴張。連續兩份通膨報告的利多，在於它們降低了近期升息的必要性，卻不以經濟急遽惡化為代價。不過，長債並未同幅受惠：短端名目殖利率下滑之際，20年期與30年期實質殖利率反而上升。

能源風險也沒有退場。美國與伊朗相關戰事持續，油價連漲第三天。聯準會理事庫克強調通膨持續偏高的風險，與主席華許、紐約聯準銀行總裁威廉斯較為樂觀的談話形成對照。信用市場仍能承接大型融資，高盛繼美元債後完成歐元債發行，QTS則擴大貸款再融資；但Altice債權人的違約通知，以及CLO評等方法可能調整，也讓市場更關注個別交易的擔保、契約保障與風險分配。

## PPI減輕升息壓力，聯準會內部仍有不同側重

6月PPI月減0.3%，低於市場原先預期的持平，年增率為5.5%；扣除食品與能源後年增4.7%，同樣低於預期。汽油價格下跌12%，能源下跌6.4%，食品則是3個月來首度下跌，運輸與倉儲成本也回落。上游價格亦有改善：扣除食品與能源的加工中間財漲幅為今年最小，電子零組件價格再度下降，國防相關價格下跌2.2%。

不過，會影響聯準會偏好的PCE物價指標的項目，表現並不一致。機票價格上漲1.9%，投資組合管理費的漲幅則放緩；批發與零售業利潤率在5月大幅下降後反彈。整份報告改善了短期通膨前景，但服務價格壓力尚未全面消退。

與此同時，7月紐約州製造業指數上升10點至15.6，新訂單與出貨指數分別達22.2、24.4，均為4年來最強；就業指數升至11.4，創2022年12月以來新高。支付價格指數下降9點至52.3，仍處偏高水準，收取價格指數為27.6。褐皮書彙整12個地區截至7月6日的資訊，也顯示經濟小幅至溫和成長、消費價格上升，各地對前景的看法不一，中東局勢帶來的能源成本仍是共同疑慮。

華許在參議院表示，AI投資推升的價格未必會形成持續性通膨，因為新增產能也能擴大供給。威廉斯認為目前政策位置合適，住宅、關稅與能源造成的價格壓力有望逐漸消退；他預估年底通膨約3.25%，到2028年回到2%。庫克更重視另一側的風險：相較於勞動市場轉弱，她目前更擔心通膨居高不下。她表示若通膨未能降溫，已準備採取行動，但仍有時間等待更多數據。

交易員則進一步押注聯準會按兵不動。7月升息機率在CPI後已降至17%以下，PPI公布後再降至約10%，相當於約3個基點的升息定價。部位調整可能放大了行情：反映7月29日決議的8月聯邦基金期貨，未平倉量自6月初以來約增至兩倍，期間累積的空單在通膨數據轉弱後面臨回補壓力。

2年期美債收在4.13%，5年期4.26%，10年期4.55%，30年期5.08%。10年期殖利率下降3個基點，使2s10s擴大2個基點至42個基點；2s30s擴大5個基點至95個基點。以一週來看，2年期已下降8個基點，30年期卻仍上升2個基點。市場撤回短期升息預期的速度，明顯快於降低長債持有報酬要求的速度。

實質殖利率曲線更清楚呈現這個落差。5年期與7年期各降2個基點至2.01%、2.15%，10年期降1個基點至2.32%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點至2.23%。但20年期與30年期實質殖利率各升1個基點，分別達2.68%、2.88%。短券也以較長天期降幅較大，52週券下降5個基點至3.97%。約$720億的119天期短券標售，得標利率為3.745%，投標倍數3.35倍；間接投標人取得60.04%，直接投標人6.13%，交易商33.83%，將於7月21日交割。

## 大額融資仍有買盤，債權保障決定個別風險

高盛週三發行€50億、分3部分的債券，加上週二的$100億美元債，約24小時內籌資超過$150億等值。歐元債訂單超過€128億，使定價較初步指引收緊逾20個基點。€12.5億浮動利率券定在3個月Euribor加78個基點，低於最初100至105個基點的指引；€20億固定利率券定在中間交換利率加68個基點，較長的€17.5億券則為加105個基點。前兩部分可於3年後首次贖回，最後一部分為7年後。強勁的交易業務表現提供支持，而繼美元債之後仍能取得深厚的歐元訂單，才是當天新增的需求訊號。

併購融資則仍在比較不同資金管道。摩根大通正為華平投資收購Pantherx安排最高$30億融資，討論中的結構包括第一、第二順位貸款，以及可能約$10億的優先股。直接貸款機構也考慮提供利率約為基準加500個基點的融資。Antares與Blue Owl先前提供、利率約為基準加450個基點的$6.2億貸款，預計維持流通。

QTS將原定貸款擴大至$32.5億、規模增至3倍以上，同時取消$10億債券發行計畫，用於資料中心組合的建設貸款再融資。這次改變融資組合前，公司過去一年已發行超過$60億投資級債。放眼整個產業，開發商自2022年底以來已籌得$1,860億永續債務資金，但地方反對在2025年使至少48項、總值$1,560億的計畫遭阻擋或延後。融資需求旺盛、債務也能順利承作，並不代表從資金到位到資產營運之間的許可與施工風險已經消失。

CLO市場的焦點則是評等機構重新檢視回收率與結構保障，而非現金流突然改善。惠譽依新準則，將304筆美國交易中的767個分券列入檢視，面額合計超過$160億；歐洲、中東與非洲地區另有132筆交易、434個分券。穆迪的提案可能使約三分之一、評等低於AAA的分券上調1至2級，部分低槓桿結構可能上調3級。過去CLO債務的違約率低於同評等公司債，次順位保障與現金流測試是重要支撐。不過，軟體業約占美國CLO貸款15%、歐洲10%，即使評等上調，對該產業變化的曝險仍然存在。

Altice International的2028年到期擔保債持有人，週二送出違約通知，指控公司涉及€50億關係企業貸款，以及將葡萄牙、多明尼加業務移出受限集團等違反契約行為。爭議核心在於資產與擔保品是否被移出債權人可追索範圍。Arini、King Street、Sona等投資人將合作協議延長至2028年1月，並研議契約及法律行動。這使既有爭端升級，但目前仍是債權人的指控，而非法院認定。

泰晤士水務面臨更迫近的資金期限。若10月初以前無法與債權人及監管機關達成協議，公司預估到2027年還需要£24億資金，現有債務則達£185億。進入特別管理程序仍屬嚴重但可能發生的情境。另一方面，ECB研究人員發現，對美出口企業的貸款需求下降、授信標準轉嚴，汽車業尤其明顯；關稅衝擊雖在2025年最強，仍持續影響銀行監控與授信決策。

大型信用債ETF隨債市上漲：LQD上升0.35%至107.58，HYG上升0.16%至79.81，JNK上升0.18%至96.07。個別交易則補足了這個正面盤勢下的差異：大型銀行有深厚需求，併購與資料中心可比較不同融資結構，資產保障有爭議的發行人則持續承受債權人壓力。

## 海外債市仍受各自的政策與供給牽動

歐洲活動數據偏弱，能源卻使政策難以直接轉向寬鬆。歐元區5月工業生產月減0.2%，前月為增加0.3%，年減幅達1.2%。能源生產增加2.2%、資本財增加0.3%，中間財減少0.3%，耐久消費財減少1.1%。ECB官員對能源衝擊的持續性仍有不同看法：納格爾重視能源價格，帕內塔強調第二輪效應，以及通膨可能直到2027年初都高於3%的風險；其他官員則尚未看到廣泛薪資效應。

挪威提供了更明確的升息預期下修理由。6月排除能源的基礎通膨為2.7%，低於央行預估的3.3%，也是約一年半來最低。8月升息定價由13個基點降至10個基點，年底前則由33個基點降至29個基點，挪威克朗兌歐元下跌0.3%。

日本長端與指標券走勢分歧。20年期殖利率上升3.5個基點至3.53%，10年期下降2個基點至2.685%。明治安田生命表示，若殖利率維持高檔，2026會計年度可加碼最多¥1兆的20年期與30年期日本公債。相較於前幾天討論的大型資產配置情境，這項有價格條件的買進意願，更能反映眼前需求。新版財政政策草案也明確提及日本銀行的政策工具及依法享有的自主性，修正先前看似限制升息的措辭，但兩項消息都還不足以消除超長債供給壓力。

法國10年期OAT殖利率達3.93%，創2009年以來新高。政府將2026年成長預估下修至0.7%，使原本就困難的赤字目標更加棘手：赤字占GDP比率需由5.1%降至5%。總統政治的不確定性也增加財政疑慮，部分投資人偏好短天期，或相對比利時減碼法債。加拿大央行則連續第6次維持利率於2.25%，預估第二季、第三季GDP年化季增率分別為2.5%、1.5%。經濟復甦、通膨逐步回到2%的預期，使央行得以繼續觀望；加拿大2年期殖利率下降約4個基點至2.83%。

## 新興市場受惠於美元轉弱，內部條件仍然分歧

美元指數下跌0.44%至100.50，加上美債殖利率下降，有利新興市場。EMB上升0.17%至95.73，新興市場貨幣指數約漲0.1%，南非蘭德、墨西哥披索表現較強，巴西里拉則因選舉疑慮落後。同樣受惠於外部環境，各國的資金成本與財政政策仍決定了不同表現。

馬來西亞3個月Klibor升至3.46%，創一年新高，較政策利率高約70個基點，年初差距約為50個基點。6月以來貸款成長快於存款，使3年期、5年期政府債的持有收益空間縮小；2035年到期公債標售的投標倍數也是今年第3低。這是經濟仍強、但融資成本提高的局面：第二季GDP預估年增5.3%，5月出口已年增45%，AI相關需求提供支持。摩根大通預估第四季升息25個基點，其他預測則顯示Klibor只會再小幅上升。

中國面對的需求問題恰好相反。6月信用擴張低於預期，政府發債放緩，即使有季底放貸誘因，民間借款需求仍弱。人民銀行要求部分銀行增加貸款，但無意大幅寬鬆。限制因素不只是資金能否取得，也包括借款人是否願意使用。

哥倫比亞本地公債自5月底以來報酬接近10%，披索接近14%，受惠於12%的政策利率、高油價，以及市場對新政府財政緊縮和債務再融資的期待，主權利差已收斂至疫情以來最低。巴西則準備向財務吃緊的農業借款人提供更多紓困：政府計畫重議超過R$1,000億農業債務，並自7月14日起暫停符合資格的付款30天，以因應連年收成與收入損失。研議中的農業保證基金可能影響未來授信，但尚未成為已落實的新保證來源。

## 油價續漲，考驗通膨利多能維持多久

S&P 500上漲0.38%至7,572.40，VIX下降5.03%至15.67，但Nasdaq 100下跌0.28%，半導體指數下跌2.08%。大盤走高之際，科技股仍偏弱。黃金也未隨較低美債殖利率及較弱美元上漲，反而下跌0.42%至$4,044。

對債市更直接的挑戰來自油價。WTI與布蘭特原油小漲至$79.60、$84.95，單週漲幅分別達8.27%、8.88%。在伊朗對科威特及荷莫茲海峽周邊加強攻擊後，美國對伊朗的攻勢持續到第5天。這次CPI、PPI反映的是較早的能源價格回落，最新一輪供應干擾仍可能在後續數據中抵銷部分改善。

美國庫存顯示，各類油品的緩衝並不相同。原油庫存下降170萬桶至4.097億桶，汽油下降150萬桶至2.105億桶；餾分油卻增加460萬桶至1.082億桶，煉油廠每日原油投入量為1,712.3萬桶。原油供應衝擊會如何傳到成品油價格，仍取決於這些差異，不能將所有油品都視為同步吃緊。

## 接下來要確認物價降溫與需求穩定能否並存

7月16日美東08:30將公布零售銷售、失業金申請與費城聯準銀行調查，可用來判斷紐約州製造業的改善是否具有代表性。7月17日08:30的進出口物價，以及09:15的工業生產，則補充進口價格與產出的資訊。若物價繼續降溫、需求保持穩定，將支持本週的行情解讀；若價格壓力重現，或活動突然明顯轉弱，就需要重新判斷債市上漲的背景。

能源與海外政策緊接其後。7月16日10:30有美國天然氣庫存，7月17日公布歐元區HICP終值，7月22日是下一份美國石油庫存報告，7月23日則是ECB決議。對歐洲而言，重要的是最新油市干擾是否延長通膨壓力，而不只是歷史數據的終值有沒有修正。

資金供給方面，7月16日11:30將標售$1,100億4週券及$1,000億8週券，7月21日交割，當日16:30另有聯準會H.4.1資產負債表。日本7月22日約¥3,000億的40年期公債標售，則將直接測試超長端需求。美國短端殖利率下降、長端實質殖利率仍高之際，這些供給事件有助於觀察買盤是否願意把持有天期拉長，而不只交易近期聯準會預期的變化。

# Softer producer prices extend the Treasury rally, but the long end holds back

## A second inflation reprieve meets a resilient economy

Treasuries rallied for a second session as a fall in producer prices reinforced the previous day's softer consumer-inflation reading. The buying remained concentrated in shorter maturities: 2- and 5-year yields fell 5 basis points, while the 30-year yield was unchanged. Traders pared the probability of a July Fed increase to about 10%, extending the retreat from roughly 40% before the CPI release.

The economic news did not point uniformly toward weaker demand. New York manufacturing orders, shipments and hiring strengthened, and the Fed's Beige Book described continued, if modest, expansion. For investors, the appeal of the inflation reports was that they reduced the immediate case for higher rates without requiring a sharp deterioration in activity. That distinction also helps explain why long-dated bonds lagged: 20- and 30-year real yields rose even as shorter nominal yields declined.

Nor had the energy risk disappeared. Oil advanced for a third day as fighting involving the US and Iran continued. Fed Governor Lisa Cook stressed the danger that inflation would persist, providing a counterpoint to the more reassuring comments from Chair Kevin Warsh and New York Fed President John Williams. Credit investors, meanwhile, were still willing to finance large transactions. Goldman's euro sale followed its US deal, and QTS enlarged a loan refinancing, while an Altice creditor notice and proposed CLO rating changes drew attention to collateral, covenants and the allocation of risk within individual structures.

## Producer prices ease; the Fed debate remains open

The June producer-price index fell 0.3% from May, against a median forecast for no change, leaving annual inflation at 5.5%. Excluding food and energy, the annual rate was 4.7%, also below expectations. Gasoline prices dropped 12% and energy fell 6.4%; food recorded its first decline in three months. Lower transportation and warehousing costs added to the relief. Further up the production chain, processed intermediate goods excluding food and energy had their slowest price increase of the year, electronic components fell again and defense-related prices declined 2.2%.

The components relevant to the Fed's preferred PCE measure were less uniformly soft. Airfares rose 1.9%, while the increase in portfolio-management fees slowed. Wholesale and retail margins rebounded after a large May decline. The release therefore improved the near-term inflation outlook without establishing that every service-price pressure was fading.

That improvement came alongside a firmer July Empire manufacturing survey. The headline index rose 10 points to 15.6; new orders reached 22.2 and shipments 24.4, their strongest readings in four years. Employment climbed to 11.4, the best since December 2022. Prices paid fell 9 points to 52.3 but remained elevated, while prices received stood at 27.6. The Beige Book, covering information collected through July 6 across all 12 districts, likewise described slight to moderate growth, higher consumer prices and uneven expectations, with Middle East energy costs a recurring uncertainty.

Warsh told the Senate that higher prices associated with AI investment need not produce persistent inflation if the resulting capacity also expands supply. Williams said the current policy stance was well positioned, citing reasons for shelter, tariff and energy pressures to fade. He expected inflation around 3.25% at year-end and a return to 2% by 2028. Cook put more weight on the other side of the risk: persistent inflation now concerned her more than a weakening labor market, and she was prepared to act if disinflation failed to emerge, while allowing time for further data.

Market pricing moved decisively toward patience. July hike odds, already below 17% after CPI, fell to about 10%, equivalent to roughly 3 basis points of tightening. Positioning may have amplified the rally. Open interest in August fed-funds futures, which capture the July 29 decision, had roughly doubled since early June as short positions accumulated; the softer inflation releases gave those positions reason to unwind.

The 2-year Treasury closed at 4.13%, the 5-year at 4.26%, the 10-year at 4.55% and the 30-year at 5.08%. The 10-year fell 3 basis points, taking 2s10s 2 basis points wider to 42; 2s30s widened 5 to 95. Over the week, the 2-year was down 8 basis points but the 30-year was still up 2. The rally was undoing front-end tightening expectations faster than it was reducing the compensation required to hold long duration.

The real-yield curve showed that difference particularly clearly. The 5- and 7-year real yields fell 2 basis points to 2.01% and 2.15%, and the 10-year fell 1 to 2.32%. The 10-year breakeven declined 2 to 2.23%. At the long end, however, 20- and 30-year real yields rose 1 basis point to 2.68% and 2.88%. Bills also repriced more at the outer end, with the 52-week yield down 5 basis points to 3.97%. A roughly $72 billion, 119-day bill auction cleared at 3.745% with 3.35 times coverage; indirect bidders took 60.04%, direct bidders 6.13% and dealers 33.83%. It settles July 21.

## Large financings clear, while collateral disputes sharpen

Goldman Sachs raised €5 billion in three parts on Wednesday, following Tuesday's $10 billion US sale and taking its combined issuance above $15 billion equivalent in about 24 hours. Euro orders exceeded €12.8 billion, allowing pricing to tighten more than 20 basis points. A €1.25 billion floating-rate tranche priced at 78 basis points over 3-month Euribor, versus initial guidance of 100–105. A €2 billion fixed-rate tranche priced at 68 basis points over mid-swaps, and a €1.75 billion longer tranche at 105. The first two are callable after three years; the last after seven. The bank's strong trading results provided a supportive backdrop, but the depth of the euro book was the new evidence of demand following the US sale.

Acquisition finance offered a different choice of channels. JPMorgan was arranging up to $3 billion for Warburg Pincus's purchase of Pantherx, with first- and second-lien debt and potentially about $1 billion of preferred equity under discussion. Direct lenders were also considering financing around 500 basis points over the benchmark. An existing $620 million loan from Antares and Blue Owl, priced around 450 basis points over the benchmark, was expected to remain outstanding.

QTS more than tripled a proposed loan to $3.25 billion and dropped a planned $1 billion bond sale as it refinanced construction debt across a data-center portfolio. The change in financing mix followed more than $6 billion of investment-grade issuance over the previous year. Across the industry, developers had raised $186 billion of sustainable debt since late 2022, yet local opposition had blocked or stalled at least 48 projects worth $156 billion in 2025. Strong financing demand and the ability to place debt did not remove the permitting and construction risks between a funding commitment and an operating asset.

In structured credit, rating agencies were reconsidering recoveries and protections rather than responding to a new wave of realized cash flow. Fitch had flagged 767 US CLO tranches, with more than $16 billion face value across 304 deals, and 434 tranches across 132 EMEA deals for review under revised criteria. Moody's proposal could lift about one-third of tranches below AAA by one or two notches, with some low-leverage structures potentially gaining three. Historical CLO debt defaults had been lower than those of similarly rated corporate bonds, supported by subordination and cash-flow tests. The exposure mix still mattered: software represented about 15% of US CLO loans and 10% in Europe, leaving meaningful exposure to changes in that sector even if ratings improved.

At Altice International, holders of secured notes due in 2028 delivered a default notice on Tuesday alleging covenant breaches involving €5 billion of intercompany loans and the transfer of Portuguese and Dominican operations outside the restricted group. The allegations center on assets and collateral moving beyond creditors' reach. Investors including Arini, King Street and Sona extended their cooperation agreement to January 2028 as they considered contractual and legal steps. The notice escalated an existing dispute; it was a creditor allegation, not a court determination.

Thames Water faced a more immediate financing deadline. Without an agreement with creditors and its regulator by early October, the utility expected to need another £2.4 billion through 2027 against £18.5 billion of debt. Special administration remained a severe but plausible scenario. Elsewhere, ECB staff found that US-facing exporters had reduced loan demand and faced tighter lending standards, particularly in autos. The tariff-related drag had been strongest in 2025 but persisted in bank monitoring and credit decisions.

Broad credit funds rose with bonds: LQD gained 0.35% to 107.58, HYG 0.16% to 79.81 and JNK 0.18% to 96.07. The individual transactions gave a more differentiated view of that constructive session—deep demand for a major bank, competing structures for acquisitions and data centers, and creditor pressure where asset protection was in dispute.

## Overseas policy and supply keep curves from moving together

Europe's activity data were soft, but energy remained an obstacle to a straightforward easing interpretation. Euro-area industrial production fell 0.2% in May after April's 0.3% increase, leaving output down 1.2% from a year earlier. Energy production rose 2.2% and capital goods 0.3%, while intermediate goods fell 0.3% and durable consumer goods 1.1%. ECB officials continued to disagree over how much of the energy shock would persist. Joachim Nagel emphasized energy prices, while Fabio Panetta highlighted second-round risks and inflation potentially above 3% until early 2027; others had yet to see broad wage effects.

Norway supplied a clearer reason to reduce tightening expectations. June underlying inflation excluding energy was 2.7%, versus the central bank's 3.3% projection and the weakest reading in about a year and a half. Pricing for August tightening fell to 10 basis points from 13, and year-end tightening to 29 from 33. The krone slipped 0.3% against the euro.

Japan's long end moved in the opposite direction to its benchmark. The 20-year yield rose 3.5 basis points to 3.53%, while the 10-year fell 2 to 2.685%. Meiji Yasuda said it could add up to ¥1 trillion of 20- and 30-year JGBs in fiscal 2026 if yields stayed high. That conditional buying interest was a more immediate guide to demand than the larger portfolio-allocation scenarios discussed in previous sessions. A revised fiscal-policy draft also explicitly referred to the BOJ's tools and respect for its legal autonomy after earlier wording had appeared to restrain rate increases. Neither development removed the supply pressure on super-long bonds.

France's 10-year OAT yield reached 3.93%, the highest since 2009. The government cut its 2026 growth forecast to 0.7%, complicating an already difficult effort to reduce the deficit to 5% from 5.1%. Presidential uncertainty added to the fiscal concern, with some investors favoring shorter maturities or an underweight relative to Belgium. In Canada, the central bank held at 2.25% for a sixth meeting, projecting annualized growth of 2.5% in the second quarter and 1.5% in the third. Its expectation of recovery and a gradual return to 2% inflation left room to hold steady; the Canadian 2-year yield fell about 4 basis points to 2.83%.

## Emerging markets gain external relief, not a common domestic outlook

A 0.44% fall in the dollar index to 100.50 and lower US yields helped emerging markets. EMB rose 0.17% to 95.73, while the EM currency index added about 0.1%. The rand and Mexican peso led gains; Brazil's real lagged amid election concerns. Domestic funding and fiscal developments continued to distinguish markets sharing the same favorable external move.

Malaysia's 3-month Klibor reached 3.46%, a one-year high and roughly 70 basis points above the policy rate, compared with about 50 at the start of the year. Loan growth had outpaced deposits since June, compressing the carry on 3- and 5-year government securities; a 2035 bond auction had the year's third-lowest coverage. This was a funding-cost constraint in an otherwise firm economy. Second-quarter GDP was expected to grow 5.3% year on year, and May exports had risen 45%, supported by AI-related demand. JPMorgan forecast a quarter-point hike in the fourth quarter, while other forecasts implied only a modest further rise in Klibor.

China faced the reverse demand problem. June credit creation missed expectations as government issuance slowed and private borrowing remained weak despite quarter-end lending incentives. The PBOC urged some banks to lend more but showed little appetite for broad easing. The issue was not simply the availability of liquidity; borrowers' willingness to use it remained subdued.

Colombian local sovereign bonds had returned almost 10% since late May, and the peso nearly 14%, supported by a 12% policy rate, high oil prices and expectations that the incoming administration would tighten fiscal policy and refinance debt. Sovereign spreads had reached their tightest since the pandemic. Brazil was moving toward additional relief for a stressed borrower group: authorities planned to renegotiate more than R$100 billion of rural debt and suspend eligible payments for 30 days from July 14 after repeated harvest and income losses. A proposed agricultural guarantee fund could influence future lending, but was not yet an established source of new guarantees.

## Oil tests the durability of the inflation rally

The S&P 500 rose 0.38% to 7,572.40 and VIX fell 5.03% to 15.67, but the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.28% and the semiconductor index 2.08%. The broader equity gain therefore coexisted with continued weakness in technology. Gold fell 0.42% to $4,044 despite lower Treasury yields and a weaker dollar.

Oil presented the more direct challenge to the bond rally. WTI and Brent edged higher to $79.60 and $84.95, taking their weekly gains to 8.27% and 8.88%. US attacks on Iran continued for a fifth day after heavier Iranian strikes involving Kuwait and the Strait of Hormuz. The CPI and PPI releases captured earlier energy relief; renewed disruption could still reverse part of it in subsequent data.

US inventories gave a mixed picture of the available cushion. Crude stocks fell 1.7 million barrels to 409.7 million and gasoline fell 1.5 million to 210.5 million. Distillates rose 4.6 million barrels to 108.2 million, while refinery inputs ran at 17.123 million barrels a day. Those differences matter for how a crude-supply shock reaches product prices: inventories were not tightening uniformly across the complex.

## The next releases must sustain both sides of the disinflation case

July 16 brings US retail sales, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey at 08:30 ET. They will show whether the stronger Empire survey is consistent with broader activity. July 17 import and export prices at 08:30 and industrial production at 09:15 will add evidence on imported inflation and output. Continued price relief alongside stable demand would reinforce this week's interpretation; renewed price pressure or a sharp loss of activity would require a different account of the rally.

Energy and overseas policy will remain close behind. US natural-gas storage is due July 16 at 10:30, final euro-area HICP on July 17, the next US petroleum report on July 22 and the ECB decision on July 23. The key question for Europe is whether the latest oil disruption alters the expected persistence of inflation, not simply whether the final historical reading changes.

Funding supply resumes with $110 billion of 4-week bills and $100 billion of 8-week bills on July 16 at 11:30, settling July 21; the Fed's H.4.1 release follows at 16:30. Japan's approximately ¥300 billion, 40-year auction on July 22 will provide a more direct test of super-long demand. With US front-end yields falling while long real yields remain firm, these supply events will help show where buyers are willing to extend beyond the immediate Fed repricing.
